name: Neuroscience Graduate Program (PhD)
detailsNote: The how-to-apply page gives December 1 for best consideration and January 1 as the final deadline without a year, so they are shown as published dates. How students are admitted (program or lab) is not stated on the pages read.
summary: Interdisciplinary Neuroscience PhD at the University of Iowa. Applicants apply through the Graduate College and select applicants are invited to interview.

publishedDeadlines.label: Best-consideration and final deadlines (year not stated)
publishedDeadlines.dateText: December 1st for best consideration with final deadline of January 1st
publishedDeadlines.note: Fall semester only. Neither page gives a year, so confirm Fall 2027.

timeline.interviews: Select applicants are contacted by email and invited for an interview in person or virtually.

english.note: International students may also be required to submit TOEFL, IELTS or DuoLingo scores. No minimum scores are listed on the pages read.

applicationFee.note: The fee is $60 ($100 for international applicants). The Graduate College grants waivers for significant financial hardship; the program cannot offer direct waivers but reimburses the fee for applicants who are invited to and complete an interview. International applicants should confirm the waiver rules.

requirements.note: Official transcripts are required before enrollment if admitted. International students recommended for admission must send a financial statement.

funding.note: The funding page says neuroscience students receive a guaranteed stipend ($36,350 for the 2026-2027 academic year), full tuition, fees and a health insurance allowance, with support beyond the first year guaranteed while progress is satisfactory. Its table is labelled 2024-2025, so confirm the current amount. It does not say whether this covers international students.
